#### Burst DMA transfers

In addition to the standard DMA requests, the HRTIM features a DMA burst controller to have multiple registers updated with a single DMA request. This allows to:

- update multiple data registers with one DMA channel only,
- reprogram dynamically one or several timing units, for converters using multiple timer outputs.

The burst DMA feature is only available for one DMA channel, but any of the 6 channels can be selected for burst DMA transfers.

The principle is to program which registers are to be written by DMA. The master timer and TIMA..E have the burst DMA update register, where most of their control and data registers are associated with a selection bit: HRTIM\_BDMUPR, HRTIM\_BDTAUPR to HRTIM\_BDTEUPR (this is applicable only for registers with write accesses). A redirection mechanism allows to forward the DMA write accesses to the HRTIM registers automatically, as shown on [Figure 285](#XREF_82471__Figure_47__DMA_burst_overview19).

<a id="XREF_82471__Figure_47__DMA_burst_overview19"></a>

#### Figure 285. ![](MS32340V1.svg)DMA burst overview

When the DMA trigger occurs, the HRTIM generates multiple 32-bit DMA requests and parses the update register. If the control bit is set, the write access is redirected to the associated register. If the bit is reset, the register update is skipped and the register parsing is resumed until a new bit set is detected, to trigger a new request. Once the 6 update registers (HRTIM\_BDMUPR, 5x HRTIM\_BDTxUPR) are parsed, the burst is completed and the system is ready for another DMA trigger (see the flowchart on [Figure 286](#XREF_66318__Figure_48__Burst_DMA_operation_flowchart19)).

**Note:**

Any trigger occurring while the burst is on-going is discarded, except if it occurs during the very last data transfer.

The burst DMA mode is permanently enabled (there is no enable bit). A burst DMA operation is started by the first write access into the HRTIM\_BDMADR register.

It is only necessary to have the DMA controller pointing to the HRTIM\_BDMADR register as the destination, in the memory, to the peripheral configuration with the peripheral increment mode disabled (the HRTIM handles internally the data re-routing to the final destination register).

To re-initialize the burst DMA mode if it was interrupted during a transaction, it is necessary to write at least to one of the 6 update registers.

<a id="XREF_66318__Figure_48__Burst_DMA_operation_flowchart19"></a>

#### Figure 286. ![](MS32341V2.svg)Burst DMA operation flowchart

Several options are available once the DMA burst is completed, depending on the register update strategy.

If the PREEN bit is reset (preload disabled), the value written by the DMA is immediately transferred into the active register and the registers are updated sequentially, following the DMA transaction pace.

When the preload is enabled (PREEN bit set), there are 3 use cases:

1. The update is done independently from DMA burst transfers (UPDGAT[3:0] = 0000 in HRTIM\_TIMxCR and BRSTDMA[1:0] = 00 in HRTIM\_MCR). In this case, and if it is necessary to have all transferred data taken into account simultaneously, the user must check that the DMA burst is completed before the update event takes place. On the contrary, if the update event happens while the DMA transfer is on-going, only part of the registers is loaded and the complete register update requires 2 consecutive update events.
2. The update is done when the DMA burst transfer is completed (UPDGAT[3:0] = 0000 in HRTIM\_TIMxCR and BRSTDMA[1:0] = 01 in HRTIM\_MCR). This mode guarantees that all new register values are transferred simultaneously. This is done independently from the counter value and can be combined with regular update events, if necessary (for instance, an update on a counter reset when TxRSTU is set).
3. The update is done on the update event following the DMA burst transfer completion (UPDGAT[3:0] = 0010 in HRTIM\_TIMxCR and BRSTDMA[1:0] = 10 in HRTIM\_MCR). This mode guarantees both a coherent update of all transferred data and the synchronization with regular update events, with the timer counter. In this case, if a regular update request occurs while the transfer is on-going, it is discarded and the effective update happens on the next coming update request.

The chronogram on [Figure 287](#XREF_92793__Figure_49__Registers_update_following_DMA_burst_transfer19) presents the active register content for 3 cases: PREEN=0, UPDGAT[3:0] = 0001 and UPDGAT[3:0] = 0001 (when PREEN = 1).

<a id="XREF_92793__Figure_49__Registers_update_following_DMA_burst_transfer19"></a>

#### Figure 287. ![](MS32342V1.svg)Registers update following DMA burst transfer

### 28.3.24 HRTIM initialization

This section describes the recommended HRTIM initialization procedure, including other related MCU peripherals.

The HRTIM clock source must be enabled in the reset and clock control unit (RCC), while respecting the fHRTIM range for the DLL lock.

The DLL calibration must be started by setting CAL bit in HRTIM\_DLLCR register.

The HRTIM master and timing units can be started only once the high-resolution unit is ready. This is indicated by the DLLRDY flag set. The DLLRDY flag can be polled before resuming the initialization or the calibration can run in background while other registers of the HRTIM or other MCU peripherals are initialized. In this case, the DLLRDY flag must be checked before starting the counters (an end-of-calibration interrupt can be issued if necessary, enabled with DLLRDYIE flag in HRTIM\_IER). Once the DLL calibration is done, CALEN bit must be set to have it done periodically and compensate for potential voltage and temperature drifts. The calibration periodicity is defined using the CALRTE[1:0] bitfield in the HRTIM\_DLLCR register.

The HRTIM control registers can be initialized as per the power converter topology and the timing units use case. All inputs have to be configured (source, polarity, edge-sensitivity).

The HRTIM outputs must be set up eventually, with the following sequence:

- the polarity must be defined using POLx bits in HRTIM\_OUTxR
- the FAULT and IDLE states must be configured using FAULTx[1:0] and IDLESx bits in HRTIM\_OUTxR

The HRTIM outputs are ready to be connected to the MCU I/Os. In the GPIO controller, the selected HRTIM I/Os have to be configured as per the alternate function mapping table in the product datasheet.

From this point on, the HRTIM controls the outputs, which are in the IDLE state.

The outputs are configured in RUN mode by setting TxyOEN bits in the HRTIM\_OENR register. The 2 outputs are in the inactive state until the first valid set/reset event in RUN mode. Any output set/reset event (except software requests using SST, SRT) are ignored as long as TxCEN bit is reset, as well as burst mode requests (IDLEM bit value is ignored). Similarly, any counter reset request coming from the burst mode controller is ignored (if TxBM bit is set).

**Note:**

When the deadtime insertion is enabled (DTEN bit set), it is necessary to force the output state by software, using SST and RST bits, to have the outputs in a complementary state as soon as the RUN mode is entered.

The HRTIM operation can eventually be started by setting TxCEN or MCEN bits in HRTIM\_MCR.

If the HRTIM peripheral is reset with the Reset and Clock Controller, the output control is released to the GPIO controller and the outputs are tri stated.

### 28.3.25 Debug

When a microcontroller enters the debug mode (Cortex®-M4 with FPU core halted), the TIMx counter either continues to work normally or stops, depending on DBG\_HRTIM\_STOP configuration bit in DBG module:

- DBG\_HRTIM\_STOP = 0: no behavior change, the HRTIM continues to operate.
- DBG\_HRTIM\_STOP = 1: all HRTIM timers, including the master, are stopped. The outputs in RUN mode enter the FAULT state if FAULTx[1:0] = 01,10,11, or keep their current state if FAULTx[1:0] = 00. The outputs in idle state are maintained in this state. This is permanently maintained even if the MCU exits the halt mode. This allows to maintain a safe state during the execution stepping. The outputs can be enabled again by settings TxyOEN bit (requires the use of the debugger).

#### Timer behavior during MCU halt when DBG\_HRTIM\_STOP = 1

The set/reset crossbar, the dead-time and push-pull unit, the idle/balanced fault detection and all the logic driving the normal output in RUN mode are not affected by debug. The output keeps on toggling internally, so as to retrieve regular signals of the outputs when TxyOEN is set again (during or after the MCU halt). Associated triggers and filters are also following internal waveforms when the outputs are disabled.

FAULT inputs and events (any source) are enabled during the MCU halt.

Fault status bits can be set and TxyOEN bits reset during the MCU halt if a fault occurs at that time (TxyOEN and TxyODS are not affected by DBG\_HRTIM\_STOP bit state).

Synchronization, counter reset, start and reset-start events are discarded in debug mode, as well as capture events. This is to keep all related registers stable as long as the MCU is halted.

The counter stops counting when a breakpoint is reached. However, the counter enable signal is not reset; consequently no start event is emitted when exiting from debug. All counter reset and capture triggers are disabled, as well as external events (ignored as long as the MCU is halted). The outputs SET and RST flags are frozen, except in case of forced software set/reset. A level-sensitive event is masked during the debug but is active again as soon as the debug is exited. For edge-sensitive events, if the signal is maintained active during the MCU halt, a new edge is not generated when exiting from debug.

The update events are discarded. This prevents any update trigger on hrtim\_upd\_en[3:1] inputs. DMA triggers are disabled. The burst mode circuit is frozen: the triggers are ignored and the burst mode counter stopped.

DLL calibration is not blocked while the MCU is halted (the DLLRDY flag can be set).

## 28.4 Application use cases

### 28.4.1 Buck converter

Buck converters are of common use as step-down converters. The HRTIM can control up to 12 buck converters with 7 independent switching frequencies.

The converter usually operates at a fixed frequency and the Vin/Vout ratio depends on the duty cycle D applied to the power switch:.![RM0440_STM32G4xx_c7amba_hrtimer1_v2_UserSpec_image653](RM0440_STM32G4xx_c7amba_hrtimer1_v2_UserSpec_image653.png)

The topology is given on [Figure 288](#XREF_68744__Figure_55__BUCK_converter_topology19) with the connection to the ADC for voltage reading.

<a id="XREF_68744__Figure_55__BUCK_converter_topology19"></a>

#### Figure 288. ![](MS32343V3.svg)Buck converter topology

[Figure 289](#XREF_26996__Figure_15__Dual_Buck_converter_management19) presents the management of two converters with identical frequency PWM signals. The outputs are defined as follows:

- HRTIM\_CHA1 set on period, reset on CMP1
- HRTIM\_CHA2 set on CMP3, reset on PER

The ADC is triggered twice per period, precisely in the middle of the ON time, using CMP2 and CMP4 events.

<a id="XREF_26996__Figure_15__Dual_Buck_converter_management19"></a>

#### Figure 289. ![](MS32344V2.svg)Dual Buck converter management

Timers A..E provide either 12 buck converters coupled by pairs (both with identical switching frequencies) or 7 completely independent converters (each of them having a different switching frequency), using the master timer as the 7th time base.

### 28.4.2 Buck converter with synchronous rectification

Synchronous rectification allows to minimize losses in buck converters, by means of a FET replacing the freewheeling diode. Synchronous rectification can be turned on or off on the fly depending on the output current level, as shown on [Figure 290](#XREF_51528__Figure_57__BUCK_converter_with_synchronous_rectification19).

<a id="XREF_51528__Figure_57__BUCK_converter_with_synchronous_rectification19"></a>

#### Figure 290. ![](MS32345V3.svg)Synchronous rectification depending on output current

The main difference versus a single-switch buck converter is the addition of a deadtime for an almost complementary waveform generation on HRTIM\_CHA2, based on the reference waveform on HRTIM\_CHA1 (see [Figure 291](#XREF_12749__Figure_58__Buck_with_synchronous_rectification19)).

<a id="XREF_12749__Figure_58__Buck_with_synchronous_rectification19"></a>

#### Figure 291. ![](MS32346V2.svg)Buck with synchronous rectification

### 28.4.3 Multiphase converters

Multiphase techniques can be applied to multiple power conversion topologies (buck, flyback). Their main benefits are:

- Reduction of the current ripple on the input and output capacitors
- Reduced EMI
- Higher efficiency at light load by dynamically changing the number of phases (phase shedding)

The HRTIM manages multiple converters. The number of converters that can be controlled depends on the topologies and resources used (including the ADC triggers):

- 5 buck converters with synchronous rectification (SR), using the master timer and the 5 timers
- 4 buck converters (without SR), using the master timer and 2 timers

[Figure 292](#XREF_59456__Figure_304__3-phase_interleaved_buck_converter19) presents the topology of a 3-phase interleaved buck converter.

<a id="XREF_59456__Figure_304__3-phase_interleaved_buck_converter19"></a>

#### Figure 292. ![](MS32347V3.svg)3-phase interleaved buck converter

The master timer is responsible for the phase management: it defines the phase relationship between the converters by resetting the timers periodically. The phase-shift is 360° divided by the number of phases, 120° in the given example.

The duty cycle is then programmed into each of the timers. The outputs are defined as follows:

<br>- HRTIM\_CHA1 set on master timer period, reset on TACMP1
<br>- HRTIM\_CHB1 set on master timer MCMP1, reset on TBCMP1
<br>- HRTIM\_CHC1 set on master timer MCMP2, reset on TCCMP1

The ADC trigger can be generated on TxCMP2 compare event. Since all ADC trigger sources are phase-shifted because of the converter topology, it is possible to have all of them combined into a single ADC trigger to save ADC resources (for instance 1 ADC regular channel for the full multi-phase converter).

#### Figure 293. ![](MS32348V2.svg)3-phase interleaved buck converter control

### 28.4.4 Transition mode power factor correction

The basic operating principle is to build up current into an inductor during a fixed Ton time. This current then decays during the Toff time, and the period is re-started when it becomes null. This is detected using a Zero Crossing Detection circuitry (ZCD), as shown on [Figure 294](#XREF_81195__Figure_64__Transition_mode_PFC19). With a constant Ton time, the peak current value in the inductor is proportional to the rectified AC input voltage, which provides the power factor correction.

<a id="XREF_81195__Figure_64__Transition_mode_PFC19"></a>

#### Figure 294. ![](MS32349V3.svg)Transition mode PFC

This converter operates with a constant Ton time and a variable frequency due the Toff time variation (depending on the input voltage). It must also include some features to operate when no zero-crossing is detected, or to limit the Ton time in case of over-current (OC). The OC feedback is usually conditioned with the built-in comparator and routed onto an external event input.

[Figure 295](#XREF_72034__Figure_23__Transition_mode_PFC_waveforms19) presents the waveform during the various operating modes, with the following defined parameters:

- Ton Min: masks spurious overcurrent (freewheeling diode recovery current), represented as OC blanking
- Ton Max: practically, the converter set-point. It is defined by CMP1
- Toff Min: limits the frequency when the current limit is close to zero (demagnetization is very fast). It is defined with CMP2.
- Toff Max: prevents the system to be stuck if no ZCD occurs. It is defined with CMP4 in auto-delayed mode.

Both Toff values are auto-delayed since the value must be relative to the output falling edge.

<a id="XREF_72034__Figure_23__Transition_mode_PFC_waveforms19"></a>

#### Figure 295. ![](MS32350V2.svg)Transition mode PFC waveforms

## 28.5 HRTIM registers

### 28.5.1 HRTIM master timer control register (HRTIM\_MCR)

Address offset: 0x000

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="118.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:30</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BRSTDMA[1:0]</span>: Burst DMA update</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define how the update occurs relatively to a burst DMA transaction.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Update done independently from the DMA burst transfer completion</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Update done when the DMA burst transfer is completed</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Update done on master timer roll-over following a DMA burst transfer completion. This mode only works in continuous mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Reserved</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MREPU</span>: Master timer repetition update</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines whether an update occurs when the master timer repetition period is completed (either due to roll-over or reset events). MREPU can be set only if BRSTDMA[1:0] = 00 or 01.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: Update on repetition disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: Update on repetition enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PREEN</span>: Preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the registers preload mechanism and defines whether the write accesses to the memory mapped registers are done into HRTIM’s active or preload registers.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: Preload disabled: the write access is directly done into the active register</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: Preload enabled: the write access is done into the preload register</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 26:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DACSYNC[1:0]:</span> DAC synchronization</p><p class="TableIndent">A DAC synchronization event can be enabled and generated when the master timer update occurs. These bits are defining on which output the DAC synchronization is sent (refer to <a href="#XREF_34054__20_3_19_DAC_triggers19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 28.3.21: DAC triggers</a> for connections details).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   No DAC trigger generated</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Trigger generated on hrtim_dac_trg1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Trigger generated on hrtim_dac_trg2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Trigger generated on hrtim_dac_trg3</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24:23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TFCEN</span>: Timer F counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the timer F counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: Timer F counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: Timer F counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit must not be changed within a minimum of 8 cycles of f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TECEN</span>: Timer E counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the timer E counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: Timer E counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: Timer E counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit must not be changed within a minimum of 8 cycles of f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TDCEN</span>: Timer D counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the timer D counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: Timer D counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: Timer D counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit must not be changed within a minimum of 8 cycles of f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCCEN</span>: Timer C counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the timer C counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: Timer C counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: Timer C counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit must not be changed within a minimum of 8 cycles of f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TBCEN</span>: Timer B counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the timer B counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: Timer B counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: Timer B counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit must not be changed within a minimum of 8 cycles of f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TACEN</span>: Timer A counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the timer A counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Timer A counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Timer A counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit must not be changed within a minimum of 8 cycles of f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MCEN</span>: Master timer counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the master timer counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Master counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Master counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit must not be changed within a minimum of 8 cycles of f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYNCSRC[1:0]</span>: Synchronization source</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the source and event to be sent on the synchronization outputs SYNCOUT[2:1]</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Master timer start</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Master timer compare 1 event</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Timer A start/reset</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Timer A compare 1 event</p></td></tr><tr height="121.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYNCOUT[1:0]</span>: Synchronization output</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the routing and conditioning of the synchronization output event.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;"><span data-conditional="_hrtim1_singleinstance">01:   Reserved</span></p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Positive pulse on HRTIM_SCOUT output (16x f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock cycles)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Negative pulse on HRTIM_SCOUT output (16x f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock cycles) </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield must not be modified once the counter is enabled (TxCEN bit set)</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYNCSTRTM</span>: Synchronization starts master</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the master timer start when receiving a synchronization input event:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect on the master timer</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A synchronization input event starts the master timer</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYNCRSTM</span>: Synchronization resets master</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the master timer reset when receiving a synchronization input event:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect on the master timer</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A synchronization input event resets the master timer</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYNCIN[1:0]</span>: Synchronization input</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are defining the synchronization input source.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Disabled. HRTIM is not synchronized and runs in standalone mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;"><span data-conditional="_hrtim1_singleinstance">01:   Reserved</span></p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Internal event on hrtim_in_sync[2]: the HRTIM is synchronized with the on-chip timer (see <a href="#XREF_97185__Synchronization_input19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Synchronization input</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   External event on hrtim_in_sync[3]: a positive pulse on HRTIM_SCIN input triggers the HRTIM.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the impacted timers are enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="177.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">INTLVD[1:0]</span>: Interleaved mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is significant only when the HALF bit is reset. It enables the interleaved mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Interleaved mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Triple interleaved mode: when HRTIM_MPER register is written, the HRTIM_MCMP1R active register is automatically updated with HRTIM_MPER/3 value, and the HRTIM_MCMP2R active register is automatically updated with 2x (HRTIM_MPER/3) value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Quad interleaved mode: when HRTIM_MPER register is written, the HRTIM_MCMP1R active register is automatically updated with HRTIM_MPER/4 value, the HRTIM_MCMP2R active register is automatically updated with HRTIM_MPER/2 value and the HRTIM_MCMP3R active register is automatically updated with 3x (HRTIM_MPER/4) value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Interleaved mode disabled</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HALF</span>: Half mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the half duty-cycle mode: the HRTIM_MCMP1R active register is automatically updated with HRTIM_MPER/2 value when HRTIM_MPER register is written.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Half mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Half mode enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RETRIG</span>: Re-triggerable mode</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit defines the behavior of the master timer counter in single-shot mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The timer is not re-triggerable: a counter reset can be done only if the counter is stopped (period elapsed)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The timer is re-triggerable: a counter reset is done whatever the counter state (running or stopped)</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CONT</span>: Continuous mode</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The timer operates in single-shot mode and stops when it reaches the MPER value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 18.43pt;">1: The timer operates in continuous (free-running) mode and rolls over to zero when it reaches the MPER value</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CKPSC[2:0]</span>: Clock prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the master timer<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll"> high-resolution</span> clock prescaler ratio.</p><p class="TableIndent">The counter clock equivalent frequency (f<sub>COUNTER</sub>) is equal to <span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">f</span><sub data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">HRCK</sub><span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll"> / 2</span><sup data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">CKPSC[2:0]</sup><sup></sup>.</p><p class="TableIndent">The prescaling ratio cannot be modified once the timer is enabled.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.2 HRTIM master timer interrupt status register (HRTIM\_MISR)

Address offset: 0x004

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MUPD</span>: Master update interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the master timer registers are updated.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No master update interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Master update interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYNC</span>: Sync input interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when a synchronization input event is received.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No sync input interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Sync input interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MREP</span>: Master repetition interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the master timer repetition period has elapsed.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No master repetition interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Master repetition interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MCMP4</span>: Master compare 4 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to MCMP1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MCMP3</span>: Master compare 3 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to MCMP1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MCMP2</span>: Master compare 2 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to MCMP1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MCMP1</span>: Master compare 1 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the master timer counter matches the value programmed in the master compare 1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No master compare 1 interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Master compare 1 interrupt occurred</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.3 HRTIM master timer interrupt clear register (HRTIM\_MICR)

Address offset: 0x008

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="118.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MCNT[15:0]</span>: Counter value</p><p class="TableIndent">Holds the master timer counter value. This register can only be written when the master timer is stopped (MCEN = 0 in HRTIM_MCR).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span><span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">For HR clock prescaling ratio below 32 (CKPSCCKPSC[2:0] &lt; 5), the least significant bits of the counter are not significant. They cannot be written and return 0 when read.</span></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The timer behavior is not guaranteed if the counter value is set above the HRTIM_MPER register value.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MPER[15:0]</span>: Master timer period value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register defines the counter overflow value.</p><p class="TableIndent">The period value must be above or equal to 3 periods of the f<sub>HRTIM </sub>clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p><p class="TableIndent">The maximum value is 0x0000 FFDF.</p></td></tr></table></div>

It is either the preload register or the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The compare value must be above or equal to 3 periods of the f<sub>H</sub><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">RTIM</span></sub><sub> </sub>clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p></td></tr></table></div>

It is either the preload register or the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The compare value must be above or equal to 3 periods of the f<sub>H</sub><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">RTIM</span></sub><sub> </sub>clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p></td></tr></table></div>

It is either the preload register or the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The compare value must be above or equal to 3 periods of the f<sub>H</sub><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">RTIM</span></sub><sub> </sub>clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MCMP4[15:0]</span>: Master timer compare 4 value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the master timer compare 4 value. It is either the preload register or the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The compare value must be above or equal to 3 periods of the f<sub>H</sub><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">RTIM</span></sub><sub> </sub>clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.12 HRTIM timer x control register (HRTIM\_TIMxCR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x080

Address offset: Block B: 0x100

Address offset: Block C: 0x180

Address offset: Block D: 0x200

Address offset: Block E: 0x280

Address offset: Block F: 0x300

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="294.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UPDGAT[3:0]</span>: Update gating</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define how the update occurs relatively to the burst DMA transaction and the external update request on update enable inputs hrtim_upd_en[3:1] (see <span data-conditional="RM0440"><a href="#XREF_84630__Table_6__Update_enable_inputs_and_sources%1119" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Table 224</a></span>).</p><p class="TableIndent">The update events, as mentioned below, can be: MSTU, TFU, TEU, TDU, TCU, TBU, TAU, TxRSTU, TxREPU.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0000:   The update occurs independently from the DMA burst transfer</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0001:   The update occurs when the DMA burst transfer is completed</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0010:   The update occurs on the update event following the DMA burst transfer completion</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0011:   The update occurs on a rising edge on hrtim_upd_en1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0100:   The update occurs on a rising edge on hrtim_upd_en2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0101:   The update occurs on a rising edge on hrtim_upd_en3</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0110:   The update occurs on the update event following a rising edge on hrtim_upd_en1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0111:   The update occurs on the update event following a rising edge on hrtim_upd_en2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1000:   The update occurs on the update event following a rising edge on hrtim_upd_en3</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">Others:    Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield must be reset before programming a new value.</p><p class="RegTNote_">For UPDGAT[3:0] values equal to 0001, 0011, 0100, 0101, it is possible to have multiple concurrent update source (for instance RSTU and DMA burst).</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PREEN</span>: Preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the registers preload mechanism and defines whether a write access into a preload-able register is done into the active or the preload register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Preload disabled: the write access is directly done into the active register</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Preload enabled: the write access is done into the preload register</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 26:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DACSYNC[1:0]</span>: DAC synchronization</p><p class="TableIndent">A DAC synchronization event is generated when the timer update occurs. These bits are defining on which output the DAC synchronization is sent (refer to <a href="#XREF_34054__20_3_19_DAC_triggers19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 28.3.21: DAC triggers</a> for connections details).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   No DAC trigger generated</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Trigger generated on hrtim_dac_trg1 </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Trigger generated on hrtim_dac_trg2 </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Trigger generated on hrtim_dac_trg3 </p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MSTU</span>: Master timer update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered by the master timer update.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update by master timer disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update by master timer enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TEU</span>: Timer E update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered by the timer E update</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update by timer E disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update by timer E enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is reserved for <span style="font-style:normal;">HRTIM_TIMECR</span>. It is only available for HRTIM_TIMACR, HRTIM_TIMBCR, HRTIM_TIMCCR, HRTIM_TIMDCR, HRTIM_TIMFCR.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TDU</span>: Timer D update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered by the timer D update</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update by timer D disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update by timer D enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is reserved for HRTIM_TIMDCR. It is only available for HRTIM_TIMACR, HRTIM_TIMBCR, HRTIM_TIMCCR, HRTIM_TIMECR, HRTIM_TIMFCR.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCU</span>: Timer C update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered by the timer C update</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update by timer C disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update by timer C enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is reserved for HRTIM_TIMCCR. It is only available for HRTIM_TIMACR, HRTIM_TIMBCR, HRTIM_TIMDCR, HRTIM_TIMECR, HRTIM_TIMFCR.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TBU</span>: Timer B update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered by the timer B update</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update by timer B disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update by timer B enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is reserved for HRTIM_TIMBCR. It is only available for HRTIM_TIMACR, HRTIM_TIMCCR, HRTIM_TIMDCR, HRTIM_TIMECR, HRTIM_TIMFCR.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TAU</span>: Timer A update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered by the timer A update</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update by timer A disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update by timer A enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is reserved for HRTIM_TIMBCR. It is only available for HRTIM_TIMBCR, HRTIM_TIMCCR, HRTIM_TIMDCR, HRTIM_TIMECR, HRTIM_TIMFCR.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TxRSTU</span>: Timer x reset update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered by timer x counter reset or roll-over to 0 after reaching the period value in continuous mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update by timer x reset / roll-over disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update by timer x reset / roll-over enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TxREPU</span>: Timer x repetition update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered when the counter rolls over and HRTIM_REPx = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update on repetition disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update on repetition enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TFU</span>: Timer F update</p><p class="TableIndent">Register update is triggered by the timer F update</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Update by timer F disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Update by timer F enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is reserved for HRTIM_TIMFCR. It is only available for HRTIM_TIMACR, HRTIM_TIMBCR, HRTIM_TIMCCR, HRTIM_TIMDCR, HRTIM_TIMECR.</p></td></tr><tr height="180.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DELCMP4[1:0]</span>: CMP4 auto-delayed mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines whether the compare register is behaving in standard mode (compare match issued as soon as counter equal compare), or in auto-delayed mode (see <a href="#XREF_16269__Auto-delayed_mode19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Auto-delayed mode</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   CMP4 register is always active (standard compare mode)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   CMP4 value is recomputed and is active following a capture 2 event</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   CMP4 value is recomputed and is active following a capture 2 event, or is recomputed and active after Compare 1 match (timeout function if capture 2 event is missing)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   CMP4 value is recomputed and is active following a capture 2 event, or is recomputed and active after Compare 3 match (timeout function if capture event is missing)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield must not be modified once the counter is enabled (TxCEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="180.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DELCMP2[1:0]</span>: CMP2 auto-delayed mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines whether the compare register is behaving in standard mode (compare match issued as soon as counter equal compare), or in auto-delayed mode (see <a href="#XREF_16269__Auto-delayed_mode19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Auto-delayed mode</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   CMP2 register is always active (standard compare mode)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   CMP2 value is recomputed and is active following a capture 1 event</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   CMP2 value is recomputed and is active following a capture 1 event, or is recomputed and active after compare 1 match (timeout function if capture event is missing)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   CMP2 value is recomputed and is active following a capture 1 event, or is recomputed and active after compare 3 match (timeout function if capture event is missing)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield must not be modified once the counter is enabled (TxCEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYNCSTRTx</span>: Synchronization starts timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines the timer x behavior following the synchronization event:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect on timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A synchronization input event starts the timer x</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYNCRSTx</span>: Synchronization resets timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines the timer x behavior following the synchronization event:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect on timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A synchronization input event resets the timer x</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RSYNCU</span>: Re-synchronized update</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit specifies whether update source coming outside from the timing unit must be synchronized:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The update coming from adjacent timers (when MSTU, TAU, TBU, TCU, TDU, TEU, TFU bit is set) or from a software update (TxSWU bit) is taken into account immediately</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The update coming from adjacent timers (when MSTU, TAU, TBU, TCU, TDU, TEU, TFU bit is set) or from a software update (TxSWU bit) is taken into account on the following reset/roll-over event.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is significant only when UPDGAT[3:0] = 0000, it is ignored otherwise.</p></td></tr><tr height="177.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 8:7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">INTLVD[1:0]</span>: Interleaved mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is significant only when the HALF bit is reset. It enables the interleaved mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Interleaved mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Triple interleaved mode: when HRTIM_PERxR register is written, the HRTIM_CMP1xR active register is automatically updated with HRTIM_PERxR/3 value, and the HRTIM_CMP2xR active register is automatically updated with 2x (HRTIM_PERxR/3) value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Quad interleaved mode: when HRTIM_PERxR register is written, the HRTIM_CMP1xR active register is automatically updated with HRTIM_PERxR/4 value, the HRTIM_CMP2xR active register is automatically updated with HRTIM_PERxR/2 value and the HRTIM_CMP3xR active register is automatically updated with 3x (HRTIM_PERxR/4) value.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Interleaved mode disabled</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PSHPLL</span>: Push-pull mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the push-pull mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Push-pull mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Push-pull mode enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield must not be modified once the counter is enabled (TxCEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HALF</span>: Half mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the half duty-cycle mode: the HRTIM_CMP1xR active register is automatically updated with HRTIM_PERxR/2 value when HRTIM_PERxR register is written.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Half mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Half mode enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RETRIG</span>: Re-triggerable mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines the counter behavior in single shot mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The timer is not re-triggerable: a counter reset is done if the counter is stopped (period elapsed in single-shot mode or counter stopped in continuous mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The timer is re-triggerable: a counter reset is done whatever the counter state.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CONT</span>: Continuous mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines the timer operating mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The timer operates in single-shot mode and stops when it reaches TIMxPER value</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The timer operates in continuous mode and rolls over to zero when it reaches TIMxPER value</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CKPSCx[2:0]</span>: HRTIM timer x clock prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the master timer<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll"> high-resolution</span> clock prescaler ratio.</p><p class="TableIndent">The counter clock equivalent frequency (f<sub>COUNTER</sub>) is equal to <span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">f</span><sub data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">HRCK</sub><span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll"> / 2</span><sup data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">CKPSC[2:0]</sup><sup></sup>.</p><p class="TableIndent">The prescaling ratio cannot be modified once the timer is enabled.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.13  HRTIM timer x interrupt status register   (HRTIM\_TIMxISR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x084

Address offset: Block B: 0x104

Address offset: Block C: 0x184

Address offset: Block D: 0x204

Address offset: Block E: 0x284

Address offset: Block F: 0x304

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">O2CPY</span>: Output 2 copy</p><p class="TableIndent">This status bit is a raw copy of the output 2 state, before the output stage (chopper, polarity). It allows to check the current output state before re-enabling the output after a delayed protection.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Output 2 is inactive</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Output 2 is active</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">O1CPY</span>: Output 1 copy</p><p class="TableIndent">This status bit is a raw copy of the output 1 state, before the output stage (chopper, polarity). It allows to check the current output state before re-enabling the output after a delayed protection.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Output 1 is inactive</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Output 1 is active</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">O2STAT</span>: Output 2 status</p><p class="TableIndent">This status bit indicates the output 2 state when the delayed idle protection was triggered. This bit is updated upon any new delayed protection entry. This bit is not updated in balanced idle.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Output 2 was inactive</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Output 2 was active</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">O1STAT</span>: Output 1 status</p><p class="TableIndent">This status bit indicates the output 1 state when the delayed idle protection was triggered. This bit is updated upon any new delayed protection entry. This bit is not updated in balanced idle.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Output 1 was inactive</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Output 1 was active</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IPPSTAT</span>: Idle push-pull Status</p><p class="TableIndent">This status bit indicates on which output the signal was applied, in push-pull mode balanced fault mode or delayed idle mode, when the protection was triggered (whatever the output state, active or inactive).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Protection occurred when the output 1 was active and output 2 forced inactive</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Protection occurred when the output 2 was active and output 1 forced inactive</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CPPSTAT</span>: Current push-pull status</p><p class="TableIndent">This status bit indicates on which output the signal is currently applied, in push-pull mode. It is only significant in this configuration.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Signal applied on output 1 and output 2 forced inactive</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Signal applied on output 2 and output 1 forced inactive</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DLYPRT</span>: Delayed protection flag</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No delayed protection interrupt occured</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Delayed Idle or balanced Idle mode entry occured</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RST</span>: Reset and/or roll-over interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the timer x counter is reset or rolls over in continuous mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No TIMx counter reset/roll-over interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: TIMX counter reset/roll-over interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RSTx2</span>: Output 2 reset interrupt flag timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to RSTx1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SETx2</span>: Output 2 set interrupt flag timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to SETx1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RSTx1</span>: Output 1 reset interrupt flag timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the Tx1 output is reset (goes from active to inactive mode).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Tx1 output reset interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Tx1 output reset interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SETx1</span>: Output 1 set interrupt flag timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the Tx1 output is set (goes from inactive to active mode).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Tx1 output set interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Tx1 output set interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CPT2</span>: Capture 2 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CPT1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CPT1</span>: Capture 1 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the timer x capture 1 event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No timer x capture 1 interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Timer x capture 1 interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UPD</span>: Update interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the timer x update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No timer x update interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Timer x update interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">REP</span>: Repetition interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the timer x repetition period has elapsed.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No timer x repetition interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Timer x repetition interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP4</span>: Compare 4 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CMP1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP3</span>: Compare 3 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CMP1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP2</span>: Compare 2 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CMP1 description</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP1</span>: Compare 1 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the timer x counter matches the value programmed in the compare 1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No compare 1 interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Compare 1 interrupt occurred</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.14 HRTIM timer x interrupt clear register    (HRTIM\_TIMxICR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x088

Address offset: Block B: 0x108

Address offset: Block C: 0x188

Address offset: Block D: 0x208

Address offset: Block E: 0x288

Address offset: Block F: 0x308

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="118.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CNTx[15:0]</span>: Timer x counter value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the timer x counter value. It can only be written when the timer is stopped (TxCEN = 0 in HRTIM_TIMxCR).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span><span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">For HR clock prescaling ratio below 32 (CKPSC[2:0] &lt; 5), the least significant bits of the counter are not significant. They cannot be written and return 0 when read.</span></p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The timer behavior is not guaranteed if the counter value is above the HRTIM_PERxR register value.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.17 HRTIM timer x period register (HRTIM\_PERxR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x094

Address offset: Block B: 0x114

Address offset: Block C: 0x194

Address offset: Block D: 0x214

Address offset: Block E: 0x294

Address offset: Block F: 0x314

Reset value: 0x0000 FFDF

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PERx[15:0]</span>: Timer x period value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds timer x period value.</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds either the content of the preload register or the content of the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The period value must be above or equal to 3 periods of the <span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">f</span><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">HRTIM</span></sub><sub> </sub>clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p><p class="TableIndent">The maximum value is 0x0000 FFDF.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.18 HRTIM timer x repetition register (HRTIM\_REPxR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x098

Address offset: Block B: 0x118

Address offset: Block C: 0x198

Address offset: Block D: 0x218

Address offset: Block E: 0x298

Address offset: Block F: 0x318

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP1x[15:0]</span>: Timer x compare 1 value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the compare 1 value.</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds either the content of the preload register or the content of the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The compare value must be either null or above or equal to 3 periods of the f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p><p class="TableIndent">The null value is programmed following the use case described in <a href="#XREF_40416__Null_duty_cycle_exception_case19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Null duty cycle exception case</a>.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.20 HRTIM timer x compare 1 compound register (HRTIM\_CMP1CxR)    (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x0A0

Address offset: Block B: 0x120

Address offset: Block C: 0x1A0

Address offset: Block D: 0x220

Address offset: Block E: 0x2A0

Address offset: Block F: 0x320

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP2x[15:0]</span>: Timer x compare 2 value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the compare 2 value.</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds either the content of the preload register or the content of the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The compare value must be above or equal to 3 periods of the <span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">f</span><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">HRTIM</span></sub><sub> </sub>clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p><p class="TableIndent">This register behaves as an auto-delayed compare register, if enabled with DELCMP2[1:0] bits in HRTIM_TIMxCR.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.22 HRTIM timer x compare 3 register (HRTIM\_CMP3xR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x0A8

Address offset: Block B: 0x128

Address offset: Block C: 0x1A8

Address offset: Block D: 0x228

Address offset: Block E: 0x2A8

Address offset: Block F: 0x328

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP3x[15:0]</span>: Timer x compare 3 value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the compare 3 value.</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds either the content of the preload register or the content of the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The compare value must be either null or above or equal to 3 periods of the f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll"> (0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,...)</span>.</p><p class="TableIndent">The null value is programmed following the use case described in <a href="#XREF_40416__Null_duty_cycle_exception_case19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Null duty cycle exception case</a>.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.23 HRTIM timer x compare 4 register (HRTIM\_CMP4xR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x0AC

Address offset: Block B: 0x12C

Address offset: Block C: 0x1AC

Address offset: Block D: 0x22C

Address offset: Block E: 0x2AC

Address offset: Block F: 0x32C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP4x[15:0]</span>: Timer x compare 4 value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the compare 4 value.</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds either the content of the preload register or the content of the active register if preload is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">The compare value must be above or equal to 3 periods of the <span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">f</span><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">HRTIM</span></sub><sub> </sub>clock<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">, that is 0x60 if CKPSC[2:0] = 0, 0x30 if CKPSC[2:0] = 1, 0x18 if CKPSC[2:0] = 2,..</span>.</p><p class="TableIndent">This register can behave as an auto-delayed compare register, if enabled with DELCMP4[1:0] bits in HRTIM_TIMxCR.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DIR</span>: Timer x capture 1 direction status</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the counting direction value when the capture 1 event occurred:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: timer is up-counting</p><p class="TableIndent">1: timer is down-counting</p><p class="TableIndent">In up-counting mode (UDM bit reset), the DIR bit is always read as 0.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CPT1x[15:0]</span>: Timer x capture 1 value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the counter value when the capture 1 event occurred.</p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

In up/down mode (UDM bit set to 1), the capture value is referred to:
- counting reset, when up-counting  
- the PER event when down counting

The DIR bit allows to discriminate the up-down phases when reading the captured value.

**Note:**

This is a regular resolution register: for HR clock prescaling ratio below 32 (CKPSC[2:0] < 5), the least significant bits of the counter are not significant. They cannot be written and return 0 when read.

### 28.5.25 HRTIM timer x capture 2 register (HRTIM\_CPT2xR)    (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x0B4

Address offset: Block B: 0x134

Address offset: Block C: 0x1B4

Address offset: Block D: 0x234

Address offset: Block E: 0x2B4

Address offset: Block F: 0x334

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DIR</span>: Timer x capture 1 direction status</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the counting direction value when the capture 1 event occurred:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: timer is up-counting </p><p class="TableIndent">1: timer is down-counting</p><p class="TableIndent">In up-counting mode (UDM bit reset), the DIR bit is always read as 0.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CPT2x[15:0]</span>: Timer x capture 2 value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the counter value when the capture 2 event occurred.</p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

In up/down mode (UDM bit set to 1), the capture value is referred to:
- counting reset, when up-counting  
- the PER event when down counting

The DIR bit allows to discriminate the up-down phases when reading the captured value.

**Note:**

This is a regular resolution register: for HR clock prescaling ratio below 32 (CKPSC[2:0] < 5), the least significant bits of the counter are not significant. They cannot be written and return 0 when read.

### 28.5.26 HRTIM timer x deadtime register (HRTIM\_DTxR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x0B8

Address offset: Block B: 0x138

Address offset: Block C: 0x1B8

Address offset: Block D: 0x238

Address offset: Block E: 0x2B8

Address offset: Block F: 0x338

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

style="font-weight:Bold;">DTFLKx</span>: Deadtime falling lock timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">This write-once bit prevents the deadtime (sign and value) to be modified, if enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Deadtime falling value and sign is writable</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime falling value and sign is read-only</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not preloaded</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 30</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTFSLKx</span>: Deadtime falling sign lock timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">This write-once bit prevents the sign of falling deadtime to be modified, if enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Deadtime falling sign is writable</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime falling sign is read-only</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not preloaded.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 29:26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SDTFx</span>: Sign deadtime falling value timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">This register determines whether the deadtime is positive (signals not overlapping) or negative (signals overlapping).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Positive deadtime on falling edge</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Negative deadtime on falling edge</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTFx[8:0]</span>: Deadtime falling value timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds the value of the deadtime following a falling edge of reference PWM signal.</p><p class="TableIndent">t<sub>DTF</sub> = DTFx[8:0] x t<sub>DTG</sub></p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTRLKx</span>: Deadtime rising lock timer x</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime rising value and sign is read-only</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not preloaded.</p></td></tr><tr read-only</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not preloaded.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p
