output to its active state.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP4</span>: Timer x compare 4</p><p class="TableIndent">Timer A compare 4 event forces the output to its active state.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP3</span>: Timer x compare 3</p><p class="TableIndent">Timer A compare 3 event forces the output to its active state.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP2</span>: Timer x compare 2</p><p class="TableIndent">Timer A compare 2 event forces the output to its active state.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMP1</span>: Timer x compare 1</p><p class="TableIndent">Timer A compare 1 event forces the output to its active state.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PER</span>: Timer x period</p><p class="TableIndent">Timer A period event forces the output to its active state.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In up/down mode (UDM bit set to 1), the counter period event is defined as per the OUTROM[1:0] bit setting.</p></td></tr><tr height="57.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RESYNC:</span> Timer A resynchronization</p><p class="TableIndent">Timer A reset event coming solely from software or SYNC input forces the output to its active state.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Other timer reset are not affecting the output when RESYNC=1.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SST</span>: Software set trigger</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit forces the output to its active state. This bit can only be set by software and is reset by hardware.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not preloaded.</p></td></tr></table></div>

Address offset: Block C: 0x1C0

Address offset: Block D: 0x240

Address offset: Block E: 0x2C0

Address offset: Block F: 0x340

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

class="TableIndent">Timer A compare 1 event forces the output to its active state.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PER</span>: Timer x period</p><p class="TableIndent">Timer A period event forces the output to its active state.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In up/down mode (UDM bit set to 1), the counter period event is defined as per the OUTROM[1:0] bit setting.</p></td></tr><tr height="57.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RESYNC:</span> Timer A resynchronization</p><p class="TableIndent">Timer A reset event coming solely from software or SYNC input forces the output to its active state.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Other timer reset are not affecting the output when RESYNC=1.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SST</span>: Software set trigger</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit forces the output to its active state. This bit can only be set by software and is reset by hardware.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not preloaded.</p></td></tr></table></div>

Address offset: Block F: 0x344

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

its active state.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Other timer reset are not affecting the output when RESYNC=1.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SST</span>: Software set trigger</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit forces the output to its active state. This bit can only be set by software and is reset by hardware.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not preloaded.</p></td></tr></table></div>

Address offset: Block D: 0x248

Address offset: Block E: 0x2C8

Address offset: Block F: 0x348

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

### 28.5.31 HRTIM timer x external event filtering register 1 (HRTIM\_EEFxR1)    (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x0CC

Address offset: Block B: 0x14C

Address offset: Block C: 0x1CC

windowing period.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>A timeout event is generated in window mode (EE1FLTR[3:0]=1101, 1110, 1111) if EE1LTCH = 0, except if the Address offset: Block F: 0x350

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 10:7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">STRTPW[3:0]</span>: Timer x start pulsewidth</p><p class="TableIndent">This register defines the initial pulsewidth following a rising edge on output signal.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield cannot be modified when one of the CHPx bits is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">t<sub>1STPW</sub> = (STRPW[3:0]+1) x 16 x t<sub>HRTIM</sub>.</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: <span data-keyref="~hrtim1_MinChopperWidth">94.1 ns</span> (1/<span data-keyref="~hrtim1_ChopperFreq">10.625 MHz</span>)</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">1111: <span data-keyref="~hrtim1_MaxChopperWidth">1.51 μs</span> (16/<span data-keyref="~hrtim1_ChopperFreq">10.625 MHz</span>)</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CARDTY[2:0]</span>: Timer x chopper duty cycle value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register defines the duty cycle of the carrier signal. This bitfield cannot be modified when one of the CHPx bits is set.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">000:   0/8 (i.e. only 1st pulse is present)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">...</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">111:   7/8</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CARFRQ[3:0]</span>: Timer x carrier frequency value</p><p class="TableIndent">This register defines the carrier frequency F<sub>CHPFRQ</sub> = f<sub>HRTIM</sub> / (16 x (CARFRQ[3:0]+1)).</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield cannot be modified when one of the CHPx bits is set.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0000:   <span data-keyref="~hrtim1_ChopperFreq">10.625 MHz</span> (f<sub>HRTIM</sub>/ 16)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">...</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1111:   <span data-keyref="~hrtim1_MinChopperFreq">664 kHz</span> (f<sub>HRTIM</sub> / 256)</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DIDL2</span>: Output 2 deadtime upon burst mode Idle entry</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit delays the idle mode entry by forcing a deadtime insertion before switching the outputs to their idle state. This setting only applies when entering in idle state during a burst mode operation.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The programmed Idle state is applied immediately to the output 2</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime (inactive level) is inserted on output 2 before entering the idle mode. The deadtime value is set by DTFx[8:0].</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled.</p><p class="RegTNote_">DIDL=1 is set only if one of the outputs is active during the burst mode (IDLES=1), and with positive deadtimes (SDTR/SDTF set to 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CHP2</span>: Output 2 chopper enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the chopper on output 2.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Output signal is not altered</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Output signal is chopped by a carrier signal</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 21:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FAULT2[1:0]</span>: Output 2 fault state</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits select the output 2 state after a fault event.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   No action: the output is not affected by the fault input and stays in run mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Active</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Inactive</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   High-Z</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled (TxCEN bit set), if FLTENx bit is set or if the output is in FAULT state.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDLES2</span>: Output 2 idle state</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the output 2 idle state.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Inactive</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Active</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter must be set prior to have the HRTIM controlling the outputs.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDLEM2</span>: Output 2 idle mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the output 2 idle mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action: the output is not affected by the burst mode operation.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The output is in idle state when requested by the burst mode controller.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is preloaded and is changed during run-time, but must not be changed while the burst mode is active.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">POL2</span>: Output 2 polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the output 2 polarity.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Positive polarity (output active high)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Negative polarity (output active low)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16:15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="105.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BIAR</span>: Balanced Idle Automatic Resume</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects is the outputs are automatically re-enabled after a balanced idle event.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is only significant if DLYPRT[2:0] = 011 or 111, it is ignored otherwise.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="345.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 12:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DLYPRT[2:0]</span>: Delayed protection</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the source and outputs on which the delayed protection schemes are applied.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">In HRTIM_OUTAR, HRTIM_OUTBR, HRTIM_OUTCR:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">000:   Output 1 delayed idle on external event 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">001:   Output 2 delayed idle on external event 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">010:   Output 1 and output 2 delayed idle on external event 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">011:   Balanced idle on external event 6 </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">100:   Output 1 delayed idle on external event 7</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">101:   Output 2 delayed idle on external event 7</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">110:   Output 1 and output 2 delayed idle on external event 7</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">111: Balanced idle on external event 7</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">In HRTIM_OUTDR, HRTIM_OUTER, HRTIM_OUTFR:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">000:   Output 1 delayed idle on external event 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">001:   Output 2 delayed idle on external event 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">010:   Output 1 and output 2 delayed idle on external event 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">011:   Balanced idle on external event 8 </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">100:   Output 1 delayed idle on external event 9</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">101:   Output 2 delayed idle on external event 9</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">110:   Output 1 and output 2 delayed idle on external event 9</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 29.76pt;">111:   Balanced idle on external event 9</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield must not be modified once the delayed protection is enabled (DLYPRTEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DLYPRTEN</span>: Delayed protection enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the delayed protection scheme.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Delayed protection is enabled, as per DLYPRT[2:0] bits</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled (TxEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTEN</span>: Deadtime enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the deadtime insertion on output 1 and output 2.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Output 1 and output 2 signals are independent.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime is inserted between output 1 and output 2 (reference signal is output 1 signal generator)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer is operating (TxEN bit set) or if its outputs are enabled and set/reset by another timer.</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DIDL1</span>: Output 1 deadtime upon burst mode idle entry</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit delays the idle mode entry by forcing a deadtime insertion before switching the outputs to their idle state. This setting only applies when entering the idle state during a burst mode operation.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The programmed idle state is applied immediately to the output 1</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime (inactive level) is inserted on output 1 before entering the idle mode. The deadtime value is set by DTRx[8:0].</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled.</p><p class="RegTNote_">DIDL=1 is set only if one of the outputs is active during the burst mode (IDLES=1), and with positive deadtimes (SDTR/SDTF set to 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CHP1</span>: Output 1 chopper enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the chopper on output 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Output signal is not altered</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Output signal is chopped by a carrier signal</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 5:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FAULT1[1:0]</span>: Output 1 fault state</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits select the output 1 state after a fault event</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   No action: the output is not affected by the fault input and stays in run mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Active</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Inactive</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   High-Z</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled (TxCEN bit set), if FLTENx bit is set or if the output is in FAULT state.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDLES1</span>: Output 1 Idle State</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the output 1 idle state.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Inactive</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Active</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter must be set prior to HRTIM controlling the outputs.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDLEM1</span>: Output 1 Idle mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the output 1 idle mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action: the output is not affected by the burst mode operation.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The output is in idle state when requested by the burst mode controller.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is preloaded and is changed during runtime, but must not be changed while burst mode is active.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">POL1</span>: Output 1 polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the output 1 polarity.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Positive polarity (output active high)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Negative polarity (output active low)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer x is enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.53 HRTIM timer x fault register (HRTIM\_FLTxR) (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x0E8

Address offset: Block B: 0x168

Address offset: Block C: 0x1E8

Address offset: Block D: 0x268

Address offset: Block E: 0x2E8

Address offset: Block F: 0x368

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLTLCK</span>: Fault sources lock</p><p class="TableIndent">0: FLT1EN..FLT6EN bits are read/write</p><p class="TableIndent">1: FLT1EN..FLT6EN bits are read only</p><p class="TableIndent">The FLTLCK bit is write-once. Once it has been set, it cannot be modified till the next system reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 30:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT6EN</span>: Fault 6 enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fault 6 input ignored</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 6 input is active and disables HRTIM outputs</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5EN</span>: Fault 5 enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fault 5 input ignored</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 5 input is active and disables HRTIM outputs</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT4EN</span>: Fault 4 enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fault 4 input ignored</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 4 input is active and disables HRTIM outputs</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT3EN</span>: Fault 3 enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fault 3 input ignored</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 3 input is active and disables HRTIM outputs</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT2EN</span>: Fault 2 enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fault 2 input ignored</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 2 input is active and disables HRTIM outputs</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT1EN</span>: Fault 1 enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fault 1 input ignored</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 1 input is active and disables HRTIM outputs</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="165.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TRGHLF</span>: Triggered-half mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines whether the compare 2 register is behaving in standard mode (compare match issued as soon as counter equal compare), or in triggered-half mode (see <a href="#XREF_84779__Triggered-half_mode19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section : Triggered-half mode</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CMP2 register is written by the user only (standard compare mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: CMP2 value is set by hardware as soon as a capture 1 event occurs. It is loaded with the     (capture 1 divided by 2) value. The initial value can be written by the user (as long as TRGHLF is</p><p class="TableIndent">    reset), but is ignored once the first capture has been triggered (the preload mechanism is</p><p class="TableIndent">    disabled for CMP2 when the TRGHLF bit is set).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield must not be modified once the counter is enabled (TxCEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">GTCMP3</span>: Greater than compare 3 PWM mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines the compare 3 operating mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 19.84pt;">0:   The compare 3 event is generated when the counter is equal to the compare value (compare match mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The compare 3 event is generated when the counter is greater than the compare value. If the     compare value is changed on-the-fly, the new compare value is compared with the current counter     value and an output SET or RESET can be generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">GTCMP1</span>: Greater than compare 1 PWM mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines the compare 1 operating mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 19.84pt;">0:   The compare 1 event is generated when the counter is equal to the compare value (compare match mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The compare 1 event is generated when the counter is greater than the compare value. If the     compare value is changed on-the-fly, the new compare value is compared with the current counter     value and an output SET or RESET can be generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="153.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FEROM[1:0]</span>: Fault and event roll-over mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines when the roll-over is generated, in up-down counting mode. It only concerns the Roll-over event used by the fault and event counters.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0 or to HRTIM_PERxR value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Event generated when the counter is equal to HRTIM_PERxR</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This setting only applies when the UDM bit is set. It is not significant otherwise.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield cannot be changed once the timer is operating (TxEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="153.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BMROM[1:0]</span>: Burst mode roll-over mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines when the roll-over is generated, in up-down counting mode. It only concerns the roll-over event used in the burst mode controller, as clock as burst mode trigger.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0 or to HRTIM_PERxR value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Event generated when the counter is equal to HRTIM_PERxR</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This setting only applies when the UDM bit is set. It is not significant otherwise.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This parameter cannot be changed once the timer is operating (TxEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="153.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ADROM[1:0]</span>: ADC roll-over mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines when the roll-over is generated, in up-down counting mode. It only concerns the roll-over event which triggers the ADC.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0 or to HRTIM_PERxR value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Event generated when the counter is equal to HRTIM_PERxR</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This setting only applies when the UDM bit is set. It is not significant otherwise.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield cannot be changed once the timer is operating (TxEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="168.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OUTROM[1:0]</span>: Output roll-over mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines when the roll-over is generated, in up-down counting mode. It only concerns the roll-over event which sets and/or resets the ouputs, as per HRTIM_SETxyR and HRTIM_RSTxyR settings.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0 or to HRTIM_PERxR value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Event generated when the counter is equal to HRTIM_PERxR</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This setting only applies when the UDM bit is set. It is not significant otherwise.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield cannot be changed once the timer is operating (TxEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="168.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ROM[1:0]</span>: Roll-over mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines when the roll-over is generated, in up-down counting mode. It only concerns the roll-over event with the following destinations: update trigger (to transfer content from preload to active registers), IRQ and DMA requests, repetition counter decrement and external event filtering.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0 or to HRTIM_PERxR value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   Event generated when the counter is equal to 0</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   Event generated when the counter is equal to HRTIM_PERxR</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This setting only applies when the UDM bit is set. It is not significant otherwise.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield cannot be changed once the timer is operating (TxEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UDM</span>: Up-Down mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines if the counter is operating in up or up-down counting mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The counter is operating in up-counting mode</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The counter is operating in up-down counting mode</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be changed once the timer is operating (TxEN bit set).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DCDR</span>: Dual channel DAC reset trigger</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines when the hrtim_dac_reset_trgx trigger is generated.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The trigger is generated on counter reset or roll-over event</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The trigger is generated on output 1 set event</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The DCDR bit is not significant when the DCDE bit is reset (Dual channel DAC trigger disabled).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DCDS</span>: Dual channel DAC Step trigger</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines when the hrtim_dac_step_trgx trigger is generated.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The trigger is generated on compare 2 event</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The trigger is generated on output 1 reset event</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The DCDR bit is not significant when the DCDE bit is reset (Dual channel DAC trigger disabled).</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DCDE</span>: Dual channel DAC trigger enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the dual channel DAC triggering mechanism.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Dual channel DAC trigger disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Dual channel DAC trigger enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be changed once the timer is operating (TxEN bit set). </p></td></tr></table></div>

data-conditional="nonuser" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td data-conditional="nonuser" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EEVBCRES</span>: External event B counter reset</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit resets the external event B counter. It is set by software and reset by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action</p><p class="TableIndent">1: External event counter B counter is reset</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="nonuser" height="72.00px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="nonuser" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td data-conditional="nonuser" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EEVBCE</span>: External event B counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the external event B counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: External event B counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: External event B counter enabled</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="nonuser" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="nonuser" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:14</p></td><td data-conditional="nonuser" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EEVACNT[5:0]</span>: External event A counter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield selects the external event A counter threshold. An event is considered valid when the number of events is equal to the (EEVACNT[5:0]+1) value.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EEVASEL[3:0]</span>: External event A Selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the external event A source.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: External event 1 is used as external event A source</p><p class="TableIndent">1: External event 2 is used as external event A source</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">9: External event 10 is used as external event A source</p><p class="TableIndent">Others: Reserved</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EEVARSTM</span>: External event A reset mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the external event x counter reset mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: External event counter A is reset on each reset / roll-over event</p><p class="TableIndent">1: External event counter A is reset on each reset / roll-over event only if no event occurs during last counting period</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EEVACRES</span>: External event A counter reset</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit resets the external event A counter. It is set by software and reset by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action<br/>1: External event counter A is reset</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EEVACE</span>: External event A counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the external event x counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: External event A counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: External event A counter enabled</p></td></tr></table></div>

class="TableIndent">Refer to TAUDIS description.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TAUDIS</span>: Timer A update disable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable an update event generation temporarily on timer A.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 19.84pt;">0:   Update enabled. The update occurs upon generation of the selected source.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 19.84pt;">1:   Update disabled. The updates are temporarily disabled to allow the software to write multiple registers that have to be simultaneously taken into account.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MUDIS</span>: Master update disable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable an update event generation temporarily.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 19.84pt;">0:   Update enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 19.84pt;">1:   Update disabled. The updates are temporarily disabled to allow the software to write multiple registers that have to be simultaneously taken into account.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BMPER</span>: Burst mode period interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when a single-shot burst mode operation is completed or at the end of a burst mode period in continuous mode. It is cleared by software writing it at 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No burst mode period interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Burst mode period interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll" height="86.67px"><td data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DLLRDY</span>: DLL Ready Interrupt Flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the DLL calibration is completed. It is cleared by software writing it at 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No DLL calibration ready interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DLL calibration ready interrupt occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1<span data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll">5</span>:7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT6</span>: Fault 6 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to FLT1 description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYSFLT</span>: System fault interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to FLT1 description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5</span>: Fault 5 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to FLT1 description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT4</span>: Fault 4 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to FLT1 description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT3</span>: Fault 3 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to FLT1 description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT2</span>: Fault 2 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to FLT1 description.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT1</span>: Fault 1 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when fault 1 event occurs. It is cleared by software writing it at 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No fault 1 interrupt occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 1 interrupt occurred</p></td></tr></table></div>

height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TA1OEN</span>: Timer A output 1 enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Setting this bit enables the timer A output 1. Writing “0” has no effect.</p><p class="TableIndent">Reading the bit returns the output enable/disable status.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared asynchronously by hardware as soon as the timer-related fault input(s) is (are) active.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: output A1 disabled. The output is either in fault or Idle state.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: output A1 enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The disable status corresponds to both idle and fault states. The output disable status is given by TA1ODS bit in the HRTIM_ODSR register.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.62 HRTIM output disable register (HRTIM\_ODISR)

Address offset: 0x398

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BMSTAT</span>: Burst mode status</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit gives the current operating state.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Normal operation</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Burst operation on-going. Writing this bit to 0 causes a burst mode early termination.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 30:23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TFBM</span>: Timer F burst mode</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to TABM description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TEBM</span>: Timer E burst mode</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to TABM description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TDBM</span>: Timer D burst mode</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to TABM description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCBM</span>: Timer C burst mode</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to TABM description.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TBBM</span>: Timer B burst mode</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to TABM description.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TABM</span>: Timer A burst mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines how the timer behaves during a burst mode operation. This bitfield cannot be changed while the burst mode is enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: TA counter clock is maintained and the timer operates normally</p><p class="TableIndent">1: TA counter clock is stopped and the counter is reset</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit must not be set when the balanced idle mode is active (DLYPRT[2:0] = 0x11).</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MTBM</span>: Master timer burst mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines how the timer behaves during a burst mode operation. This bitfield cannot be changed while the burst mode is enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Master Timer counter clock is maintained and the timer operates normally</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Master Timer counter clock is stopped and the counter is reset</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BMPREN</span>: Burst mode preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the registers preload mechanism and defines whether a write access into a preload-able register (HRTIM_BMCMPR, HRTIM_BMPER) is done into the active or the preload register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Preload disabled: the write access is directly done into active registers</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Preload enabled: the write access is done into preload registers</p></td></tr><tr height="310.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BMPRSC[3:0]</span>: Burst mode prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">Defines the prescaling ratio of the f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock for the burst mode controller. This bitfield cannot be changed while the burst mode is enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0000:   Clock not divided</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0001:   Division by 2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0010:   Division by 4</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0011:   Division by 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0100:   Division by 16</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0101:   Division by 32</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0110:   Division by 64</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0111:   Division by 128</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1000:   Division by 256</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1001:   Division by 512</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1010:   Division by 1024</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1011:   Division by 2048</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1100:   Division by 4096</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1101:   Division by 8192</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1110:   Division by 16384</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1111:   Division by 32768</p></td></tr><tr height="262.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 5:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BMCLK[3:0]</span>: Burst mode clock source</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the clock source for the burst mode counter. It cannot be changed while the burst mode is enabled (refer to <span data-conditional="RM0440"><a href="#XREF_21255__Table_7__Burst_mode_clock_sources_from_general_purpose_time19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Table 225</a></span> for on-chip events 1..4 connections details).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0000:   Master timer counter reset/roll-over</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0001:   Timer A counter reset/roll-over</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0010:   Timer B counter reset/roll-over</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0011:   Timer C counter reset/roll-over</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0100:   Timer D counter reset/roll-over</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0101:   Timer E counter reset/roll-over</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0110:   On-chip event 1 (hrtim_bm_ck1), acting as a burst mode counter clock</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0111:   On-chip event 2 (hrtim_bm_ck2) acting as a burst mode counter clock</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1000:   On-chip event 3 (hrtim_bm_ck3) acting as a burst mode counter clock</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1001:   On-chip event 4 (hrtim_bm_ck4) acting as a burst mode counter clock</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1010:   Prescaled f<sub>HRTIM</sub> clock (as per BMPRSC[3:0] setting)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">1011:   Timer F counter reset/roll-over</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">Others: Reserved</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BMOM</span>: Burst mode operating mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit defines if the burst mode is entered once or if it is continuously operating.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Single-shot mode</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Continuous operation</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BME</span>: Burst mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the burst mode controller which becomes ready to receive the start trigger.</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing this bit to 0 causes a burst mode early termination.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Burst mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Burst mode enabled</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.65 HRTIM burst mode trigger register (HRTIM\_BMTRGR)

Address offset: 0x3A4

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

### 28.5.66 HRTIM burst mode compare register (HRTIM\_BMCMPR)

Address offset: 0x3A8

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.29px"/><col width="540.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BMCMP[15:0]</span>: Burst mode compare value</p><p class="TableIndent">Defines the number of periods during which the selected timers are in idle state.</p><p class="TableIndent">This register holds either the content of the preload register or the content of the active register if the preload is disabled.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>BMCMP[15:0] cannot be set to 0x0000 when using the <span style="font-style:normal;">f</span><sub><span style="font-style:normal;">HRTIM</span></sub> clock without a prescaler as the burst mode clock source (BMCLK[3:0] = 1010 and BMPRESC[3:0] = 0000).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 28.5.67 HRTIM burst mode period register (HRTIM\_BMPER)

Address offset: 0x3AC

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_hrtim1_dll"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="73.07px"/><col width="539.22px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CALRTE[1:0]</span>: DLL Calibration rate</p><p class="TableIndent">This defines the DLL calibration periodicity.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: 1048576 * t<sub>HRTIM </sub>(6.168 ms for f<sub>HRTIM</sub> = 170 MHz)</p><p class="TableIndent">01: 131072 * t<sub>HRTIM </sub>(771 µs for f<sub>HRTIM</sub> = 170 MHz)</p><p class="TableIndent">10: 16384 * t<sub>HRTIM </sub>(96 µs for f<sub>HRTIM</sub> = 170 MHz)</p><p class="TableIndent">11: 2048 * t<sub>HRTIM </sub>(12 µs for f<sub>HRTIM</sub> = 170 MHz)</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CALEN</span>: DLL Calibration Enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the periodic DLL calibration, as per CALRTE[1:0] bit setting. When CALEN bit is reset, the calibration can be started in single-shot mode with CAL bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Periodic calibration disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Calibration is performed periodically, as per CALRTE[1:0] setting</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CALEN must not be set simultaneously with CAL bit</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CAL</span>: DLL Calibration Start</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit starts the DLL calibration process. It is write-only.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No calibration request</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Calibration start</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CAL must not be set simultaneously with CALEN bit</p></td></tr></table></div>

enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to FLT5E description.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5LCK</span>: Fault 5 lock</p><p class="TableIndent">The FLT5LCK bit modifies the write attributes of the fault programming bit, so that they are protected against spurious write accesses.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is write-once. Once it has been set, it cannot be modified till the next system reset.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: FLT5E, FLT5P, FLT5SRC[1:0], FLT5F[3:0] and FLT5BLK bits are read/write.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: FLT5E, FLT5P, FLT5SRC[1:0], FLT5F[3:0] and FLT5BLK bits cannot be written (read-only mode)</p></td></tr><tr height="360.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 6:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5F[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Fault 5 filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the frequency used to sample FLT5 input and the length of the digital filter applied to FLT5. The digital filter is made of an event counter in which N events are needed to validate a transition on the output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0000:   No filter, FLT5 acts asynchronously</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 36.85pt;">0001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; ### 28.5.79 HRTIM burst DMA timer x update register (HRTIM\_BDTxUPR)    (x = A to F)

Address offset: Block A: 0x3DC

Address offset: Block B: 0x3E0

Address offset: Block C: 0x3E4

Address offset: Block D: 0x3E8

Address offset: Block E: 0x3EC

Address offset: Block F: 0x3F4

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT6BLKE</span>: Fault 6 blanking enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to FLT5BLKE description.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5RSTM</span>: Fault 5 reset mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the FAULT5 counter reset mode</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fault 5 counter is reset on each reset / roll-over event</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 5 counter is reset on each reset / roll-over event only if no fault occurred during last counting period.</p><p class="TableBodyL">Note: This bitfield is written only when FLT5E enable bit is reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5CRES</span>: Fault 5 counter reset</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit resets the FAULT5 counter. It is set by software and reset by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 5 counter is reset</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 5:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5CNT[3:0]</span>: Fault 5 counter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield selects the FAULT5 counter threshold. A fault is considered valid when the number of events is equal to the (FLT5CNT[3:0]+1) value.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5BLKS</span>: Fault 5 blanking source</p><p class="TableIndent">The FTL5BLKS bit selects the FAULT5 blanking source (refer to <a href="#XREF_96068__Table_34__Fault_input_blanking_events19" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Table 252</a> for details).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fault 5 reset-aligned blanking window</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 5 Moving blanking window</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield is written only when FLT5E enable bit is reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FLT5BLKE</span>: Fault 5 blanking enable</p><p class="TableIndent">The FTL5BLKE bit selects the FAULT5 blanking mode. The blanking source is defined by the FLT5BLKS bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No blanking on fault 5</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fault 5 blanking mode</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield is written only when FLT5E enable bit is reset</p></td></tr></table></div>
